newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Filipinos protest in support of S.Korean strikers.
newsitem.headline: Filipinos protest in support of S.Korean strikers.

text.p: Filipino workers and students picketed the South Korean embassy in Manila on Friday to show their support for South Korean workers who have launched crippling strikes to protest against a new labour law.
"We are here to support the struggle of the working class in South Korea," said Manuel Sarmiento, secretary-general of the militant Philippine labour group, the May First Movement.
The new labour law, which grants South Korean companies the right to lay off surplus workers, hire temporary staff and replace strikers, has sparked widespread protests in South Korea.
The Filipino protesters, chanting slogans and carrying placards, blamed South Korean president Kim Young-sam for what they said was escalating discontent of the working class in his country.

"Your presidency will find only itself to blame should the crisis escalate," May First Movement leader Crispin Beltran said in a letter to the South Korean president, which was handed over at the embassy.

"The workers are merely asserting their trade union and democratic rights. They have done so after the anti-worker and anti-union labour laws and the anti-democratic National Security Planning Agency Act were treacherously passed by your government," the letter said.
